text:
pagerduty-bot: URGENT: P0 — multiple nodes in inference-pool-west-2a moved to NotReady (kubelet restart). Pager duty escalation to oncall: maya. :rotating_light:

maya: I’m on it. seeing ~8 nodes in inference-pool-west-2a NotReady, a few pods CrashLoopBackOff. Paging infra.

raj: hitting the pool — kubelet restarts with kernel messages about nv_peer_mem and then CUDA driver errors. nodes: ip-10-0-23-45, ip-10-0-23-47, ip-10-0-23-60.

sam: can you paste pod names? I want runtimes logs — might be GPU driver OOM / illegal address.

raj: pods affected: infer-runner-5f8d7, infer-runner-6b9a2, model-server-b7c9c. quick logs:

```
model-server-b7c9c stderr: 2026-03-15T12:04:21Z runtime: cudaErrorIllegalAddress: device kernel failed
model-server-b7c9c stderr: 2026-03-15T12:04:22Z runtime: kernel launch failed: out of memory
```

maya: ok so combo of cuda errors + kubelet restarting. likely kernel driver flake causing kubelet to kill pods as node goes NotReady. immediate mitigation: move traffic off the pool and cordon the flaky nodes.

ops-bot: Command acknowledged: cordon ip-10-0-23-45; cordon ip-10-0-23-47; cordon ip-10-0-23-60.

maya: starting drain on remaining NotReady candidates to avoid scheduling new pods. Doing a temporary traffic steer to inference-fallback-usw (CPU-backed) until we stabilize — will increase latency but reduce errors.

kelly: heads up — Customer telemetry shows a spike in 99th latency for high-throughput customers using the t-stream route. Engineers notified, CS informed.

sam: running kubectl describe node ip-10-0-23-45 output: kubelet restarted 3x in last 10m; dmesg shows "NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00:00: Xid (PCIe) 79: GPU has fallen off the bus". suspect driver/hardware flake.

raj: confirm gpu-driver version is 535.12; we rolled that platform-wide last week. trying to repro on spare node.

maya: plan: 1) cordon/drain impacted nodes 2) scale up warm nodes in dedicated-warm pool with older driver (533.x) 3) update routing policy to prefer the warm pool 4) run live canary of model-server on warm nodes 5) after stabilization, replace nodes with repro image and rejoin.

sam: executing step 2 now: autoscaler bumped dedicated-warm by +6. I'll label them with taint: inference-temporary:NoSchedule so we can control placement.

raj: collecting crashlogs -> saved to s3://redwood-incident/1768459999/gpu-crash-ip-10-0-23-45.log. snippet:

```
[ 12:03:18 ] NVRM: Xid (PCIe) 79: timeout, GPU locked
[ 12:03:19 ] kernel: NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 12:03:20 ] kubelet: NodeController: Node ip-10-0-23-45 status NotReady
```

maya: good. also enabling prefix-cache flush on routing to avoid stale KV references during migration.

kelly: CS checking impacted customers. preliminary list: two enterprise tenants on streaming gen and one mid-market on batch embeddings. No ingestion data loss, only latency/errors. Marking sev2 customer impact for customers using realtime route.

sam: live-test on new warm node: deployed model-server v2 (same binary) -> sanity tests pass, quick 1k token generation tests stable. launching gradual traffic handoff.

ops-bot: Traffic route update: inference-pool-west-2a -> inference-fallback-usw (weight 0.6) applied.

maya: traffic shift started. monitoring SLOs. If latency or error rates climb, we’ll fallback to CPU-only for affected customers and open an ETA for remediation.

raj: is there a kernel OOM killer signature? Checking dmesg for oom_reaper — nothing obvious. This looks like PCIe GPU reset failures. I'll open a ticket with our cloud provider host ops and request hardware repro.

sam: also noticed occasional container crash with stack: "kv-cache panic: invalid pointer" immediately after GPU error — suspect the serving runtime didn’t handle device reset gracefully. filing bug: INF-4312.

maya: good catch. add it to post-incident report. For immediate fix, we should patch runtime to catch cudaErrorIllegalAddress and gracefully restart worker thread; but that’s medium-term. For now, keep nodes cordoned and let new warm nodes serve.

kelly: CS update: customers A and B notified with interim mitigation notes and ETA for next update in 30 minutes. No SLA credit requests yet.

raj: cloud provider replied — host-level NIC firmware mismatch could cause GPU resets; they’re scheduling a host replacement for ip-10-0-23-45. ETA 2 hours.

maya: OK. Action items: - keep nodes cordoned - continue traffic steer until warm pool stable - collect all GPU logs and dmesg (raj) - runtime bug triage (sam) - customer comms (kelly)

sam: I'm running a quick hotfix: rolling restart of model-server with increased retry/backoff around device allocations to reduce cascading crashes. Pushing now to canary set.

ops-bot: Deploy accepted: model-server hotfix -> canary (3 pods).

maya: Metrics: error rate dropping from 12% -> 2% in 10m since traffic shift. 99th latency up 200ms for routed customers. Not ideal but stable.

kelly: noted. updating CS with degraded performance window.

raj: collecting node replacement plan after host swap. after hosts replaced, we’ll run a soak test before rejoining to inference-pool-west-2a.

maya: thanks team. I’ll keep this thread open. If anything changes, ping and we’ll escalate to infra lead. :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by oncall (maya). Current status: mitigation in progress.

maya: closing loop for now — last_message. will file postmortem with timeline and root cause once cloud confirms hardware vs driver.
